Okay, so, house tour, part two. Nothing here is complicated, I promise. Breakfast is whenever you want, but if you take the last of the milk, you have to write it on the board by the fridge. That board is the only rule I really care about. You don't have to eat dinner with us every night, but we do eat together around seven, and Emma will complain loudly if you skip it. On school nights we ask everybody to be home by ten, and on Fridays and Saturdays it's midnight. If you're going to be late, you don't need permission, you just need to text. And you can use the washing machine any time except after nine at night, because the wall is thin and my wife sleeps early.

Hi Lais, it's Maya, Greg's wife. I'm at work until six today, so I'll leave a note for you here. You don't have to cook anything tonight, there are leftovers from yesterday in the blue container. Please take them out of the fridge around half past six so they are not freezing. Two small things. You are allowed to invite friends over, of course, but let one of us know in the morning, not when they are already at the door. And could you put your laundry basket outside your room on Sundays? I do a big wash on Sunday evenings and it is easier if everything is in one place. That's it. See you at dinner.

Greg shows Lais the board by the fridge and explains the milk rule. He tells her that the family eats dinner together at around seven. Lais asks what time she has to be home on school nights. Greg says ten on school nights and midnight at the weekend. Lais asks whether she is allowed to invite a friend over on Saturday.
